method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file again. That covered title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (9 lines, with its two new mitmachen glosses) and its gist item, and the three inputs: the LS1 class dialogue (10 lines), the LS2 web page with 10 lines, and the LS3 e-mail with the 10-line office scene. It also covered the 9 LS4 texts (announcements of 34/37/32/31 words and signs of 21/19/18/19/19 words, recounted), both strategy cards, the 8 redemittel with their function labels, both Aussprache blocks, and the three rule cards the unit shows (rc.perfekt-sein, rc.wollen, rc.verbposition-2). On the speaking side we read the Sp1+Sp2 task: instructions, situations, cards, persona, openingLine, 8 hintWords and 16 model turns. On the writing side we read the S2 task: situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist and the 33-word model text. We also read the Fokus card, the fact record, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de, and the 24 u12 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json (the word cards). We solved all 102 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: start gist 1, input 15, structured input 12, pool 33, reserve 15, perception 8, exam 9, check 8 and proof 1. We permuted every sentence-building tile set and tried every one-word and one-move correction. We ran 44 candidate answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js; the results are quoted in previousFindings, F02 and notes. We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (node scripts/course-v2/compile.mjs a1.1 --out <scratch> --banks-out <scratch>), so nothing was written to the repo. We then ran the server's normalizeSpeakingTask and buildCoursePartnerPrompt (netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs) on the compiled a11-u12-s entry (F01). We scanned every German string against knownForms(a1.1, 12) from scripts/course-v2/lib-validate/lexicon.mjs. That scan included the surfaces the validator does not walk: the Fokus card, facts, redemittel labels, the Aussprache focus and the persona (F08). We checked exam fidelity against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: h2 has 4 × R/F, 1 play and textWords [29, 47]; l3 has 5 × R/F on signs with their location and [10, 25]; sp1 is a monologue with spelling and a number; sp2 is cards-ask with 2 rounds; s2 has 3 Leitpunkte and about 30 words, with Anrede and Gruß outside the Leitpunkte. We checked cast and story against casts/series.json, casts/a1.json and u01–u11. Priya: 28; Malayalam, Englisch, Deutsch; hobby Musik/tanzen as in u08; phone 0176 38 29 41 06 as in u02 and u08. Emre: Elektrogeschäft in İzmir, wife Elif in Leipzig. Arta: online from Prishtina, husband in Leipzig since childhood, an evening learner. Bilal Ahmed: from Lahore, Chancenkarte. Frau Schulz: from Leipzig. The Folge continues u11's cliffhanger „Wer macht mit?“, and the cliffhanger is the series beat a1.1-u12 → a1.2-u01. We read the rails r1 proposed at their source (ITM-01.mjs correctionFamily, lib-validate/orders.mjs, metalanguage.mjs walkReadSurfaces, detectors.json det.genitiv-feminin-attribut) to report which exist. The non-exam three-option keys sit at a 11 / b 11 / c 13, so the u04 r4-F03 class does not recur.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 8 MINOR. The r1 fixes landed well. Of r1's 15 findings, 13 are fixed or fixed in the unit, one is partly fixed (F15: the unit fallback is in, the lexicon part is open), and one is open with its owner (F14). The validator is green. All 102 keys are right. Both answers r1 found rejected are now accepted, the can-do proof needs German, and Priya's number matches u02 and u08. The genitives, the redemittel labels, the timetable breaks and the calques are gone. Three findings stop exit. (1) F01, BLOCKER, not owned by the unit. This is the engine class of u01, u08 and u10 r2-F01. The fokus Teil sd1.sp1 is run and scored correctly. The AI never runs Teil 2, however, and nothing scores it, while the proofs of cd.a1.lernziele and cd.a1.herkunft-situation are elicited only by Teil 2's cards. (2) F02, MAJOR, owned by the unit. It is a residue of our own r1-F12 proposal. The key of l3-02 depends on reading „auch dort“ as 'not here', so under the SD1 R/F convention a candidate can defend falsch. One promptDe and one explanation fix it. (3) F03, MAJOR, owned by the rule cards. rc.verbposition-2, which LS3 shows, still models „Was sprechen Sie?“ (u01 r2-F04). The eight minors: F04, receptive nouns the unit makes the learner write (Monat, Kurs). F05, a listening item whose distractors are never heard. F06, a deixis slip in Arta's line. F07, a structured-input item solved by the name before „will“. F08, the level's first Fokus-Karte, written with B1 words and no glosses. F09, a cliffhanger that presupposes a hotel never mentioned. F10 and F11, two owner items carried from r1 (rc.perfekt-sein; lexicon examples). The unit's own edits are six small ones: l3-02, ls1-i04, ls2-l05, ls2-s01, the Fokus title plus one word, and one sentence in ls2-l10.

exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, every criterion at 4 or above and at most 5 logged MINOR. F01 is the gate, and the unit does not own it: the E1 server track must read `parts` and score each Teil with its own profile (u01 r2-F01). F03 needs one row of rc.verbposition-2 changed, the same edit that closes u01 r2-F04. F02 is one promptDe and one explanation in the unit. With these three, D, A and P return to 4. After the unit edits for F05, F06, F07 and the unit parts of F08 and F09, four owner-held minors remain (F04, the SCHEMA part of F08, F10 and F11), which is within the limit. Then re-read l3-02, ls1-i04, ls2-l05, ls2-s01, ls2-l10 and the Fokus card, and run checkItem on the new ls1-i04 and ls2-s01. Stop-the-line (§9.4) is in force for four classes that recur in three or more a1.1 units: the speaking engine drops `parts` (u01, u04, u05, u06, u08, u09, u10, u12); rule cards are false or unnatural (u01, u04, u08, u10, u12); receptive lemmas must be produced (u04, u08, u10, u12); and distractors are never heard (u04, u10, u12).

findings.problem: This is the engine class of u01 r2-F01, u08 r2-F01 and u10 r2-F01. u01 r2 already listed u12 among the affected units, and nothing in speakingAI.mjs has changed. In u12 the Prüfungsfokus is intact: the fokus Teil sd1.sp1 is parts[0], so it is run as a monologue and scored with its own profile. But two of the three 'sprechen' proofs are elicited only in Teil 2. cd.a1.lernziele („was ich mit Deutsch machen möchte“) is asked only by Nora's card „Plan“ („Was wollen Sie mit Deutsch machen?“). The home-country half of cd.a1.herkunft-situation is asked only by her card „Land“ („Wo haben Sie in Ihrem Land gearbeitet?“). The Teil 1 keywords (Name … Hobby) elicit neither, and in SD1 „Beruf?“ elicits the current job. In the running session the AI gets the monologue script and is told to add one or two follow-up questions, which the persona spends on the Familienname and the phone number. It never runs the card rounds, although its own opening line announces „Teil 2 mit den Karten“ and SpeakingTaskView shows the learner both Teile with their cards. Whether the AI reaches the two Teil 2 questions at all is left to chance. speakingV2 grades the whole transcript with sd1-sp1 (vorstellen, buchstabieren, nummer; max 3). The learner's two card questions (2 points each in sd1-sp2) and answers have no criterion. So the Das-kann-ich tick of two can-dos rests on a Teil that is neither run nor scored. That is a scorer on the wrong pass rule for Teil 2, and a can-do claimed but not performed in the product (§9.4 BLOCKER). Both can-dos are practised in ls1-mo and ls2-mo, but the proofs point at the Aufgabe, and that is right for productive-spoken can-dos. No unit-side mitigation exists, because the engine also drops the parts' situationDe. The class affects eight a1.1 units (u01, u04, u05, u06, u08, u09, u10, u12), so it is stop-the-line.

findings.proposedRule: The u01 r2-F01 test over every compiled speaking bank entry with `parts`: (a) the partner prompt contains one ABLAUF per part and every part's learner and partner cards; (b) the grading plan covers every part's profile; (c) every can-do whose proof is an Aufgabe is elicited by a part that (a) and (b) cover. Add a11-u12-s to the failing fixtures (with a11-u01-s, a11-u04-s, a11-u08-s and a11-u10-s). The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: t6 „Kurs A1 von Frau Schulz: Heute nicht hier! / Bitte gehen Sie in Kursraum 2. / Die Wörterbücher sind auch dort.“ · l3-02 „An Kursraum 5: „Die Wörterbücher sind heute nicht hier.““ → richtig · explanation „Auf dem Schild steht: „Die Wörterbücher sind auch dort.“ „dort“ ist Kursraum 2, nicht hier in Kursraum 5.“ · checkItem(„falsch“) → wrong
findings.problem: This is a residue of our own r1-F12 proposal. The sign says only that the dictionaries are „auch dort“, i.e. also in room 2, with the course. It does not say that they are not in room 5. „auch dort“ can just as well be read as 'there as well'. In an SD1 richtig/falsch Teil, a statement the text does not support is falsch. A careful candidate can therefore defend falsch, and the explanation has to add a step the sign does not state. Lesen Teil 3 at A1 tests explicit information, not an implicature of „auch“. The statement also lifts „heute nicht hier“ verbatim from the sign's first line, where it is said of the course, not of the dictionaries. So the word-spotter r1-F12 set out to stop still scores this item. §9.4: an ambiguous item is MAJOR.
findings.fix: l3-02 promptDe „An Kursraum 5: „Heute ist der Kurs von Frau Schulz nicht in Kursraum 5.““ (72 characters; 11 words in the statement; key richtig unchanged, so the L3 keys stay F R F R F). The learner must link „hier“ to the location label, which is the skill the L3 strategy card names („Lesen Sie zuerst die Aussage und den Ort“). explanation.de „An Kursraum 5 steht: „Heute nicht hier!“ Der Kurs ist heute in Kursraum 2.“ (14 words). t6 stays unchanged; its dictionary line becomes a detail. Every word is known at u12 (lx.kursraum since u06).
findings.proposedRule: None beyond r1-F12's ITM-04 bound, which is still unwritten. That bound (a richtig statement shares no content-word trigram and at most two content words besides names and numbers with its text) would have flagged the lifted „heute nicht hier … Wörterbücher“. (2) Grammatical orders marked wrong (u04 r1-F04): every Vorfeld and Mittelfeld order the tiles build is accepted. (3) Dictation sources with `say` (u04 r2-F01): the six sources and c05 are plain lines. (4) Number words rejected in number gaps (u04 r3-F01): „zehn“, „dreihundertzwanzig“ and „3“ are accepted. (5) lex.articlePlural sources without a plural (r3-F03) and lex.glossTyped sources on receptive lemmas (r4-F02): all sources are productive, and the nouns have regular plurals. (6) Exam texts off-band (r1-F10): H2 34–37 words, L3 18–21. (7) Protagonists in LS4 texts (r2-F06): announcers and signs only. (8) A bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ (r5-F01): every correction names its category. (9) Genitives on task surfaces (r5-F05): none are left. (10) Skewed a/b/c keys (r4-F03): a 11 / b 11 / c 13. (11) Proof items solvable from the stem (r1-F06): q01 now needs „dann“ = later. (12) Factual claims without facts[] (r4-F05): the Österreich/Schweiz record is current, sourced and lists its exceptions. (13) Word-spotting R/F keys (r1-F19): h2-03 and l3-04 now paraphrase, and l3-02 is F02.

Exemplar classes that DO recur: the speaking engine drops `parts` (u01 r2-F01 → F01). A rule card that is unnatural or false (u01 r2-F04, u04 r2-F09 … r5-F04 → F03, F10). Receptive lemmas that must be produced (u04 r4-F02, u10 r2-F03 → F04). Distractors never heard (u04 r1-F19, u10 r2-F08 → F05). A structured-input key found in the stem (u04 r1-F26, r2-F03 → F07). Word cards above the ceiling (u04 r4-F01 → F11). F02 is a residue of our own r1 proposal, and we name it as such.

Checked and not raised. (1) ls1-p10 and ls1-r04 reject a correction that also moves a phrase into the Vorfeld („Nach Leipzig bin ich geflogen.“ and „In Kochi hat Priya am Empfang gearbeitet.“ → wrong, tagged perfekt-aux-participle). The prompt asks „haben oder sein?“, so the minimal correction is the right key. For consistency with the unit's other five corrections, the Vorfeld order could be added with acceptedWhy. The error tag misroutes a learner whose auxiliary is right; that is for the checker owner. (2) „Wieviel“ in ls3-p02 is the pre-1996 spelling, and the item grades it CORRECT. Without the listing, checkItem grades it WRONG, not TYPO. The cleaner fix is a checker TYPO for a missing space, not a listed variant. The LEX-03 advisory on it is noise, because accepted alternatives are not production models. (3) Frau Schulz „Nur einmal bin ich ins Ausland gefahren. Nach Wien“: the cast bible gives her Leipzig, Englisch and Russisch and no travel history, so nothing contradicts it. (4) c08 can be answered by matching heard words, but it is a listening Check item, not a proof. (5) ls3-s01 to ls3-s04 test W-word meaning under g.verbposition-2, whose spine label covers W-Fragen. (6) h2-03's „billig“ follows from „im Angebot“ plus „nur 1,50 Euro“. (7) In ls1-l07, „zu Hause“ for two online learners is literal. (8) The LS6 Leitpunkt „Warum lernen Sie Deutsch?“ can be answered without weil, as the model text shows, and u08 uses the same pattern. (9) The S2 theme, an e-mail to a school about a course, is a generic SD1 topic. The wording and the Saturday course are original. The agent proxy blocks the Goethe Modellsatz, so no verbatim comparison was possible. (10) Arta's evening online course (ls2-l06) matches her cast arc („lernt abends nach der Arbeit“).

We checked every proposed fix against the rails before recommending it. F02's statement has 11 words (sentence maxWords 12) and 72 characters (examStemChars [15, 90]), and it keeps the L3 keys F R F R F. F05's options are one form class, the key stays in position b, and the explanation has 17 words. F07's prompt has 82 characters (TXT-04 ≤ 90), and its explanation has 12 words. F09's new ls2-l10 sentences have 7 and 8 words. Every word in the unit-side fixes is known at u12 or is metalanguage („Teil“), except „Hotel“, which F09 glosses.

Legal and claims: no surface promises an outcome. The Folge now says „mit einem Plan lernen Sie gut“, and the web page says the course is „richtig für Sie“, not that it guarantees a pass. No surface claims human feedback or misuses exam marks. The AI partner is „Nora — Teilnehmerin in der Prüfung“ and in Teil 1 the „Gesprächsleitung (KI)“; it is never called a Prüferin. The 4 announcements, 5 signs, the Sp cards and the S2 situation are original in the SD1 format, and both strategy cards and the block instructions are paraphrases. The one fact record is current (read 2026-09-27) and lists its exceptions.
